text: P1 holds data_product_access and no masking row. The masking rows, the role list and the permission matrix are rwb-access's (Ownership Map v1: masking_rule, role and permission to P4) and are reached only through POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise and the FieldMasker interface of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, one hop with a 2 s timeout; no query of rwb-source-data names masking_rule, role, permission or retention_rule.
why: TSD P1 v3 T3.6 keeps masking_rule in P1's schema and describes P1 applying the mask, while the Ownership Map and Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 give the masking policy to P4 and R5.4 makes a table have one owner, so one of the two readings must lose.
read: Ownership Map v1 table masking_rule to P4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 DP-08 and R-PREC; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 and T6.3; legacy RWB-E1-016 sections 7 and 12 (FieldMasker published by RWB-E1-037)
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access product owner at the wave 1 contract review
impact: The three stories are buildable as written against the P4 fake from Day 1; if P4 keeps the masking rows in another service, the authorise and FieldMasker contract is the only thing that changes and no P1 table, index, view or seed row is affected.

text: Version DPA-2026.11 is seeded with the six rows the sources give and no other row: RW-CASEOWN on DP02, RW-AUDIT on DP02, and RW-PHONECOL on DP01, DP02, DP03 and DP05, all with can_read true, valid_from 2026-11-20 and a null valid_to. No DP06 row is written for RW-PHONECOL, because the legacy story refuses that read for want of a row.
why: The sources give only these rows and no role-to-product matrix, so the rest of the version cannot be derived; seeding a guess would grant or refuse access the data steward never approved.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-016 section 3 precondition and AC3 and AC5; FSD P1 v3 A2.15.2, A2.15.3.2 and A2.15.4 AC-ALT-P1-015-01 and AC-ALT-P1-015-02; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 data_product_access and T6.3

impact: Every access criterion of the app story runs on these six rows; a role or product left out of the seed is refused until a later approved load, which is the safe direction, and the gap is closed by one load through the reference-data contract.

text: The access load arrives as reference data for table code data_product_access through the rwb-case reference-data contract, and rwb-source-data implements the reference-table handler that validates the whole version and applies it; the service exposes no load endpoint of its own.
why: The monolith reference-load endpoint has no target and reference data is rwb-case's by the R-PREC default ruling and DP-07, while the approved rows still have to reach the service that owns data_product_access.

applied_in: RWB-P1-E1016-APP sections 3, 4, 8, 12.2, 12.8 and 19; RWB-P1-E1016-CON sections 3, 7, 12.2 and 12.8

text: The DB slice of this legacy key is the three indexes on data_product_access, sys_fields and sys_objects, the read model v_data_product_catalog, the DPA-2026.11 seed, the 122 object and 1,366 field conformance check and the schema checks; it creates no table, because RWB-P1-E1001-APP and RWB-P1-E1069-DB already create the tables this legacy key names.
why: The Work Package gives the DB story no object list and two other stories already own the DDL, so without a fixed boundary the DB story would either duplicate a table on the same sequence or deliver nothing provable.
read: RWB-P1-E1001-APP sections 1, 4 and 12.7; RWB-P1-E1069-DB section 12.7; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29; WP B-P1-01 story line RWB-P1-E1016-DB; TSD P1 v3 T3.6

impact: The DB story is small and testable and the sequence keeps one creator per table; if the platform instead expects the DB story to own the DDL, the indexes, the view and the seed move with it and the app story is unchanged.

text: The case list is read by contract, not by file. The extract file, the outbound file adapter, the lake path and the Power BI data set 'Case list v1' are removed under DP-17, and the released rows are served to rwb-case for SCR-02 and to rwb-reporting for its measures through GET /case-list/dates/{businessDate} and GET /case-list/rows, or through the snapshot(page) activity for a caller inside the namespace. The publish_status gate of RWB-P1-E1011-APP is kept as the release point, so a HELD date answers its status and no rows. Legacy AC2 is read as the columns, the three filters and the refresh line of those answers, every legacy value kept; legacy AC9 is kept as history, with the PUBLISHED check answering YES for a RELEASED date and NO for a HELD one and no exception-queue task, because there is no transfer left to fail.
why: Arch v5 removes the data lake and INT-19 and INT-20, while the legacy story ends with a CSV extract through the outbound file adapter and a 07:30 Power BI refresh; without a stated replacement two legacy criteria would name artefacts no target has.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-002 section 4 steps 9 and 10, section 7 AC2 and AC9, section 12, section 13; TSD P1 v3 T5.1 row INT-19; Arch v5 slides 2, 7, 15, 37 and 42; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-17
applied_in: RWB-P1-E1002-APP section 1, section 2, section 5 X5, section 7 Target reading of AC2 and AC9, section 12.2, section 12.9, section 13, section 17; RWB-P1-E1002-CON section 2, section 7 AC7, section 12.9, section 19; RWB-P1-E1002-OPS section 7 AC1, section 12.9, section 13 capacity
confirm: Data architect and the reporting owner at the wave 1 design review
impact: Two legacy criteria change shape rather than value, and no lake credential, adapter, mount or data-set job is deployed; the release point stays the reconciliation hold.

text: The case-list read path is fixed as two REST operations and one activity. GET /case-list/dates/{businessDate} answers businessDate, publishStatus, rowCount and refreshedAt, and answers 404 for a date with no run. GET /case-list/rows answers a page of rows in the 19-column order DF-RPT-001 to DF-RPT-019, filtered by businessDate, team, queue and product. The snapshot(page) activity takes the business date and the page number and returns the same rows to rwb-case and rwb-reporting inside the namespace. Both operations sit under /api/recovery/source-data/v1 with Reporting R, are read only, and are also reached through the gateway-bff composite route. The maximum page size, the sort key and the JSON types of the row answer stay open for the contract baseline review.
why: No source gives the operations that serve the released case list: TSD P1 v3 lists four P1 operations and none is a case-list read, Arch v5 names snapshot(page) without a shape, and the ownership ruling keeps the case list API with rwb-case while the row table stays with P1.
read: Arch v5 slides 15 and 41; TSD P1 v3 appendix T-A.1; FSD P1 v3 A2.18; plan ownership ruling ASM-A6-tables-2; Template and Rules v1 section R7.2 s12
applied_in: RWB-P1-E1002-APP section 11, section 12.1, section 12.5, section 12.9, section 13; RWB-P1-E1002-CON section 7 AC1, section 11, section 12.1, section 12.5; RWB-P1-E1002-OPS section 7 AC7, section 12.1
confirm: Solution architect, the rwb-case owner and the reporting owner at the contract baseline review
impact: The build story has fixed shapes to code against and rwb-case and rwb-reporting have one paged read path; a page size or sort change is an additive contract change.

text: The daily case-list build is CaseListBuildWorkflow, one run per business date with workflow ID = business date, started by rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 and otherwise by the DailyCaseList Schedule at 07:15 Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and a one-business-date catch-up window. The 07:15 fallback is the legacy caselist.allocation.wait.until value kept unchanged, read through the rwb-case parameter contract and never written into a values file. The two activities are listEligibleAccounts, which reads the case through the rwb-case case query and allocation contracts, and snapshot(page), which reads P1's own released rows.
why: Arch v5 names JOB-04 as an event-triggered workflow in rwb-source-data and names only its activities; no source gives the workflow name, the schedule name or the fallback time, so the four stories of this key would otherwise register different names for the same daily build.
read: Arch v5 slides 15 and 44; TSD P1 v3 T4 and T5.3; legacy RWB-E1-002 section 3 and section 7 AC6
applied_in: RWB-P1-E1002-APP section 1, section 3, section 4, section 5 X2, section 7 AC6, section 12.5, section 12.6, section 13; RWB-P1-E1002-CON section 7 AC6, section 12.5, section 12.6; RWB-P1-E1002-OPS section 7 AC5, section 12.5, section 12.6
confirm: Solution architect and the platform workflow owner at the wave 1 design review
impact: One workflow and one schedule name across the build, contract, operations and integration stories; the fallback time stays a parameter, so a change is a reference load and not a release.

text: The Ownership Map is applied to RWB-E1-017: retention_rule, retention_action, the retention load and its approval and the monthly Schedule JOB-17 belong to P5 rwb-document; rwb-source-data holds no rule table, registers no Schedule, receives the rule version, the run date and the rules in the run request, validates them against its own tables and applies them to interaction, case_list_row, reconciliation_result, data_product_load, party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext and valuation_ext.
why: TSD P1 v3 T3.6 still defines retention_rule as a P1 table while the Ownership Map rules retention to P5 and Architecture v5 slide 44 puts JOB-17 in rwb-document; the higher source in R-PREC wins and the loser is recorded.

text: The retention-run surface of rwb-source-data is fixed as POST /retention-runs and GET /retention-runs/{runId} on /api/recovery/source-data/v1, with Idempotency-Key on the start, 202 with a runId, 409 for an active run date, 422 for a refused rule set, and an answer carrying the status, the counts per table, the rule version, the archive location and the held cases.
why: No source names an operation by which another service starts a retention run on rwb-source-data or reads its record, and the legacy story starts it internally.
read: RWB-E1-017 sections 4, 5 and 12; Architecture v5 slide 15; Ownership Map API list for P1; TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.1

text: The archive of a run is written to the write-once container of RWB-PLT-TE012-APP under retention/YYYY-MM-DD/<table>/ with a manifest of the row count and the SHA-256 per file, using the service's own credential and the container's immutability policy; the container's own request shape, credential scope and manifest schema stay with RWB-PLT-TE012-APP.
why: The legacy story fixes the path and the manifest content but the container contract is owned by RWB-PLT-TE012-APP and is absent from the source documents read here.

text: The freshness stamp takes source_extracted_at from v_ace_batch_status.started_at and loaded_at from v_ace_batch_status.completed_at, following FSD P1 A2.14.2 with its open point OQ-P1-04 and the legacy rule, and not the mapping of TSD P1 T3.6.
why: Two sources disagree on the same two columns. The TSD ranks above the FSD under R-PREC, but its entry is a single-cell mapping with no rule behind it, the FSD carries the open point that settles the source time, and the legacy acceptance criterion asserts both values; the reading that keeps every legacy value is therefore taken and the conflict is recorded as CG-B-P1-01-E1015-1.
read: TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.6 and T3.7; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.14.2 and A2.14.3; legacy RWB-E1-015 AC1, section 4 step 2 and section 11.
applied_in: ?4 Flow step 3, ?11 Data, ?12.3 Events published, ?7 Target reading
confirm: Data steward and the P1 tech lead; the TSD author corrects T3.6 in its next version.
impact: No behaviour change against the legacy story; a stamp whose source time were completed_at would report every product as extracted at the moment it finished and would make the reported age of the data wrong.

text: AceDataReady and AceDataLate are CloudEvents 1.0 messages in Kafka binary mode carrying the seven payload fields eventId, occurredAt, schemaVersion, sourceSystem, businessDate, status and completedAt, with subject set to the source system and the attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype; both are keyed by sourceSystem and businessDate, and the contract security scheme names 'the rwb_source_data login (DP-02)'.
why: Architecture v5 fixes the transport, the envelope standard, the producer and the consumers of this tuple but names no attribute for it, TSD P1 T5.3 fixes the payload only, and no source names the login; the platform envelope is therefore applied as published, the key follows the only facts the event carries, and the login is referenced by its DP-02 role.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 15 and 43; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T5.3; Template and Rules v1 ?R5.5 DP-09, DP-14 and DP-02.

confirm: Platform event owner and the P1 tech lead.
impact: The four consuming services and rwb-decision build against one envelope and one payload from Day 1; a later refinement of an attribute is an additive change inside version 1.

text: There is one cut-off Temporal Schedule per source-fed data product, named from the product code, firing at data_product.expected_by in Asia/Bangkok with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and the per-product expected-by values beyond the two seeded rows (08:00 for the daily products and MON 08:00 for DP06) are catalog data loaded by the data steward rather than values fixed in this key.
why: Architecture v5 slide 44 fixes a Schedule per job with overlap SKIP and a catch-up window and the legacy story fixes one trigger per product, but no source names a Schedule, lists the remaining expected-by values or sizes the catch-up window; the catalog is already the declared home of the two values that are known, and BR7 of the story forbids a value in code.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 44; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.7; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.14.2; legacy RWB-E1-015 section 3 and section 12.
applied_in: ?12.6 Schedules, ?11 Data, ?15 Screens and states, and the operations story ?12.6 and ?13 capacity
confirm: Data steward and the platform administrator.
impact: No code change when a cut-off moves; the registration step reads the data row, and a product without sources gets no Schedule at all.

text: The target has no data lake: the two reconciliation extracts of legacy INT-19, the Power BI report 'Reconciliation and data quality' and its 07:30 refresh are removed, and the results are read through GET /admin/reconciliation/results and GET /admin/reconciliation/results/{resultId} on /api/recovery/source-data/v1 (API-P1-003), which rwb-reporting calls for its dashboards (DP-17). The legacy sentences that name the lake are kept word for word as history and are read as the release of the case list for the read path of RWB-P1-E1002-APP.
why: Architecture v5 slides 2 and 37 remove the lake connection and DP-17 retires INT-19 and INT-20, while the legacy story, the FSD P1 v3 A2.12 and the TSD P1 v3 T5.1 still describe two extracts and a report that reads them; without a stated read path the slice has no deliverable and the report has no source.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 4, 5, 12, 13 and 15; FSD P1 v3 A2.12; TSD P1 v3 T5.1 and T-A.2 API-P1-003; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2, 37, 44 and 45; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-17.
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-reporting owner at the Service Contract Catalog review
impact: Two file interfaces and one report become two REST reads; no lake row, no extract and no refresh exists in any story of this key, and no behaviour of the checks changes.

text: P1 owns REC-01, REC-02 and REC-05 over its own tables only (case_list_row, interaction, party_ext, contact_point_ext, account_ext, valuation_ext). REC-01 and REC-02 write one reconciliation_result row per product group each, REC-05 lists its orphans as breaks and writes no result row, and the fifteen-row count of the legacy criteria is read as five checks over three product groups. REC-03, REC-04 and the REC-05 keys of rwb-case, rwb-asset and rwb-comms belong to RWB-P3-E1011-APP, RWB-S5-E1011-APP and RWB-P6-E1011-APP.
why: The Change Register splits the legacy key by service, the Ownership Map gives treatment to S2 and proceeds to P8, and the boundary rule forbids P1 reading another service's table, while TSD P1 v3 still describes the three checks and a cross-estate REC-05 inside the P1 module; the count of rows cannot be both six and fifteen.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-011 sections 4, 8, 11 and 16; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 and T-A.2 API-P1-003; FSD P1 v3 A2.11 and A2.12; Change Register v1 row RWB-E1-011; ownership.json (treatment S2, proceeds P8, reconciliation_result P1); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-01.
confirm: Tech leads of rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-asset and rwb-comms at the wave 1 scope review
impact: P1 writes six rows per business date instead of fifteen; the treatment, payment and cross-service checks are built and tested in their own services, and no service reads another's table.

text: The reconciliation is exposed as GET /admin/reconciliation/results and GET /admin/reconciliation/results/{resultId} on /api/recovery/source-data/v1 with the result elements mapped to DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129, the run is ReconciliationWorkflow with workflow ID recon-{businessDate} and the activity reconciliation on task queue rwb-source-data in namespace rwb-recovery, and the published interface behind the reads is ReconciliationQuery.
why: API-P1-003 gives one operation, its filters and an array answer and no more, Architecture v5 names the workflow 'reconciliation' without a contract, and the legacy story has no REST surface at all, so the app, the operations story and rwb-reporting cannot be built or contract-tested without one agreed path and one agreed shape.
read: TSD P1 v3 T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P1-003 and T3.6; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15 and 44; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 DP-10 and DP-11 and R7.2 section 12.
confirm: Solution architect and the platform workflow owner at the Service Contract Catalog review
impact: An element rename is one contract version and one client; the field IDs, the operation identifier API-P1-003 and the behaviour do not change.
